hypotheses.text: Seizure penetrance, semiology (ranging from febrile seizures to infantile spasms), and age of onset do not significantly differ between carriers of the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant and carriers of unique non-recurrent missense variants within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain of KLHL20.
hypotheses.rationale: Because 11 of the 14 discovery cohort individuals carry the identical de novo p.Gly357Arg substitution while the remaining 3 carry private missense variants that also cluster within the Kelch-type beta-propeller substrate-binding domain, it is critical to determine whether the incomplete penetrance and variable semiology of seizures is an allele-specific quirk of p.Gly357Arg or an intrinsic feature of Kelch domain disruption.

evidence.text: The 14 discovery patients carrying de novo KLHL20 missense variants include 11 with the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant and 3 with unique missense variants, all clustering within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain and exhibiting overlapping phenotypes including intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder
source.quote: We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type β-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein, which shapes the substrate binding surface.

evidence.text: ClinGen curation records indicate that individuals with heterozygous KLHL20 variants display seizures spanning febrile seizures and infantile spasms, documented across both the 11 individuals with p.Gly357Arg and other Kelch-domain missense cases.

hypotheses.text: Non-recurrent missense variants located outside of the Kelch-domain substrate-binding blade (e.g., in the BTB or BACK domains) confer a milder neurodevelopmental profile with negligible epilepsy risk compared to Kelch-domain mutations.
hypotheses.rationale: All 14 reported pathogenic de novo missense variants in the index series cluster exclusively within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain. If variants outside this domain retain partial substrate adapter function, individuals with non-Kelch variants may present with non-syndromic autism or intellectual disability without early-onset seizures.

evidence.text: All 14 identified individuals with pathogenic de novo missense variants in KLHL20 carried substitutions clustering strictly within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain; no pathogenic de novo missense variants were confirmed in the BTB or BACK domains in the initial cohort.

hypotheses.text: The high recurrence of c.1069G>A (p.Gly357Arg) is primarily attributable to a hypermutable CpG dinucleotide mutational hotspot rather than differential phenotypic severity compared to other Kelch-domain missense changes.
hypotheses.rationale: In the discovery cohort, 11 of 14 independent families harbored the exact same c.1069G>A transition. Differentiating whether this overrepresentation reflects higher intrinsic germline mutability or ascertainment bias driven by a more dramatic, fully penetrant seizure phenotype is essential for counseling and diagnosis.

evidence.text: The recurrent variant observed across 11 unrelated individuals is NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.(Gly357Arg), which occurs at a CpG dinucleotide site in KLHL20.

new_directions.rationale: Extracting the exact individual-level tabular data from Table 1 and Supplementary Tables of Sleyp et al. (2022) will definitively resolve whether seizure penetrance deviates between p.Gly357Arg carriers and private Kelch-domain missense carriers.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-recurrent missense variants in KLHL20 affect the same substrate-docking electrostatic residues as p.Gly357Arg in the Kelch beta-propeller, and do in vitro ubiquitination assays demonstrate equivalent functional deficits?
new_directions.rationale: Understanding the functional biochemistry of p.Gly357Arg versus the other three Kelch domain variants will establish whether phenotypic variability in seizure severity stems from variable substrate degradation kinetics.
